title: Review: Polarisation; Reflection and refraction; Single-slit diffraction; Superposition, interference and coherence; Young's double slit; Diffraction grating
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W06-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W07-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W04-1#N.9a, W06-1#N.2a, W07-1#N.6a, W08-1#N.12, W09-1#N.8a, W04-1#N.6a, W06-1#N.12, W07-1#N.2, W09-1#N.10, W06-1#N.8, W07-1#N.9a, W09-1#N.4a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Zero order
items.clue: Straight-through beam, white for white light because every λ has θ = 0 there.

items.label: Ray
items.clue: Line perpendicular to the wavefronts, showing the direction the energy travels.

items.label: Laser
items.clue: Source giving a narrow, intense beam of coherent light; ideal for interference.

items.label: Diffraction
items.clue: Spreading out of light as it leaves each narrow opening, so the two beams overlap.

questions.stem: A ray of light passes from air into a transparent liquid. The incident ray makes an angle of 40.0° with the surface of the liquid and the refracted ray makes an angle of 55.0° with the surface. The speed of light in air is 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the speed of light in the liquid?

Two pulses of identical shape and size but opposite displacement travel towards each other along a stretched string. At one instant they overlap exactly and the whole string is momentarily straight. Which statement about this instant, and what follows it, is correct?

options.text: The pulses have cancelled each other out; the string stays straight from now on.
The string is straight but moving; the pulses then emerge and continue past each other.
The string is straight and at rest; the pulses' energy has become internal energy of the string.
The pulses have collided; each then travels back the way it came, with its shape restored.

questions.stem: In a Young's double-slit experiment, monochromatic red light is incident normally on the slits and the fringe separation on the screen is 2.0 mm. Which single change would make the fringe separation 4.0 mm?

options.text: Doubling the distance between the centres of the slits
Using blue light, of shorter wavelength, in place of the red
Halving the width of each slit, keeping their separation
Halving the distance between the centres of the two slits

questions.stem: Sea waves reach a harbour wall with a 20 m wide entrance. A boat is moored behind the wall, well to one side of the entrance. On day 1 the waves have a wavelength of 20 m; on day 2, 2.0 m, with the same amplitude. On which day is the boat rocked more, and why?

options.text: Day 1: the wavelength is about the width of the gap, so the waves spread widely.
Day 2: shorter waves have a higher frequency, so they carry more energy around the wall.
Neither: the gap is the same width both days, and the gap alone sets the spreading.
Day 2: shorter waves fit through the gap more easily, so more of them pass behind it.

questions.stem: Predict first. White light is incident normally on a diffraction grating. Which describes the pattern seen on a screen?

options.text: A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and violet nearest the centre
A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and red nearest the centre
A spectrum at the centre, as well as in each order on either side, with violet nearest to the centre
A white central maximum and a white maximum in each order, as all colours share the same angles

questions.stem: The refractive index of a certain plastic is 1.5. Which statement correctly describes what this value means?

options.text: Light travels 1.5 times as fast in the plastic as in a vacuum.
The plastic's density is 1.5 times the density of water.
A ray entering from air is bent to 1/1.5 of its angle of incidence.
Light travels 1.5 times as fast in a vacuum as it does in the plastic.

questions.stem: Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ

questions.stem: Predict first. Monochromatic light passes through two very narrow slits and falls on a distant screen, producing a pattern of bright and dark bands. Which explanation accounts for this pattern?

options.text: Light travels straight through the slits, and each bright band is an image of a slit.
Light spreads out from each slit, and the waves from the two slits overlap and interfere.
Light is refracted at the edges of each slit, which bends it into separate bright bands.
Waves from the two slits interfere where they meet, so no spreading at the slits is needed.

questions.stem: A laser beam is directed normally at a grating with 500 lines per mm. On a screen 1.00 m from the grating, the two second-order spots are 1.50 m apart. What is the wavelength of the laser light?

options.text: 750 nm
600 nm
832 nm

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.

questions.stem: Laser light passes through two slits 0.25 mm apart onto a wall 2.50 m away. A student measures across six fringe spacings: the fringes span 39.0 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing = 39.0 mm ÷ 6 = 6.5 mm. λ = slit separation × fringe spacing ÷ slits-to-screen distance = (0.25 × 10⁻³ × 6.5 × 10⁻³)/2.50 = 6.5 × 10⁻⁷ m: red light.

questions.stem: Light of wavelength 650 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating that has 600 lines per millimetre. At what angle to the straight-through direction is the second-order maximum observed?
